It was requested that I share a couple of recipes that I use for my own beard conditioner and oils, so here we are. As mentioned in the other thread, there really isn't anything exciting or complex about the process. It's just a matter of putting the items together and then using them (like any recipe I suppose).

Beard Conditioner

The beard conditioner/wax is as simple as mixing some unbleached beeswax with a base oil (I prefer coconut because it is solid at room temps). The percentages you use of each is entirely up to your own desires. I began with a 50/50 mix initially and then played with a little more of each component to get what I liked in consistency If you want a harder wax, use more beeswax. If you want more of a conditioner to soften your beard and give it more luster, use more oil. There are alternatives to coconut oil if you are allergic or don't prefer the coconut smell (such as shea/cocoa butter). Alternatives to beeswax if you cannot get it would be something like carnuba. You can also mix your waxes to get a different smell/consistency to your liking as well as oils.

My final ratio ended up being about 60% beeswax to 40% coconut oil. It makes a firm wax that melts nicely in your hand with a little rubbing.

For scents, you'll want to focus on essential oils. They aren't cheap, but you don't have to use a lot (though I'd suggest adding them after your wax has finished on the stove and has begun to cool down. You don't want to destroy the essential oils.). I settled on lime for the conditioner, so it ended up with a coconut-lime scent. It gives you beard a nice feel and can help knock down those strays that we all know happen when you let your beard grow long.

Beard Oil

The beard oil is a similar process, though you're using only oils for ingredients. You could use coconut oil, again, though you're going to end up with a result that firms up at room temps (so that's a plus if you prefer it). I settled for a base of hemp oil. You can get it pretty much at any health oriented section of a store, though I found it was cheaper to order off of Amazon. For the scents, again you want to use essential oils (because they don't break down if you protect them from UV rays using amber or completely opaque containers).

Some of the essential oils that I use for my oils that people seem to like:<br /> Lime

  • Coconut
  • Sandlewood
  • Ceder
  • Clove
  • Rosemary
  • Thyme
  • Nag Champa

For the ratios, of course it is personal preference, though essential oils go a long way. For a small vile (1-2oz), 5-7 drops or less can give you a nice faint scent that can hold all day long and not overwhelm the people around you. When I did the coconut/lime oil, I used much less lime because the lime is potent (I ended up using 3 drops from an eye dropper in about 2oz of base oil and about 5-6 drops of the coconut because it's more gentle).

I apologize that I can't give a 1:1 recipe for what I did myself, but it's all about experimenting in both percentages of ingredients and combinations of scents. I have combined many of the oils I use and found that rosemary and clove gives a nice masculine smell without being overly potent... but remember: clove essential oil has a big scent, so keep it under control and don't overdo it! :)

I hope this helps some of you undertake the idea of making your own conditioners and oils. It's not a difficult thing to do, and you get to tailor your scents to the smells you like instead of what a store decides you should wear. Some of the combinations I prefer myself are rosemary/clove, rosemary/thyme, coconut/lime, sandlewood/clove, ceder/lime. It's all about creating a custom smell that you like that will set your beard apart from others!
